title: Tamsin and the Ember
premise: Rafael Ashgrove, gatekeeper turned charm-seller in the magic-outlawed city of Correnvale, receives a dying stranger's map and discovers it leads to the Ember: the living flame that binds King Aldous to the usurper Veyra, who wears his crown and commands his armies. Tamsin, a smuggler with her own debts to the stranger, becomes his reluctant guide through the free cities as Veyra's hunters close in. Betrayals within their small company force Rafael to choose between loyalty to those who saved him and the truth that one of them carries the Ember's spark — and that destroying the Ember may kill the king they mean to save. In the end, Rafael unbinds Aldous by letting the Ember pass into himself, paying the price of survival with his own magic and memory, while Tamsin chooses truth over loyalty and exposes Veyra before the free cities' council.
about_author: Yara Pemberton is a former archivist from the Cornish coast who writes fantasy about ordinary people caught in extraordinary bargains. Her short fiction has appeared in several small-press anthologies; 'Tamsin and the Ember' is her first novel.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Seven years after sealing the Ashgrove gate, Rafael sells harmless charms in Correnvale, hiding his gift from the Wardens. A routine sale goes wrong when Warden inspectors raid his stall. The beat is quiet dread: a man surviving by making himself small.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A wounded man collapses against Rafael's shop door at night, pressing a bloodstained map into his hands and whispering 'the Ember burns where the crown was made.' Wardens kill the stranger in the street. Rafael is left holding proof of magic — terror and reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: Tamsin of the Salt Road
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Smuggler Tamsin intercepts Rafael fleeing the city, recognizing the map as the one her missing brother died carrying. She offers passage south in exchange for it. The beat is wary negotiation between two people both lying about what they want.

chapters.title: What the Map Shows
chapters.summary: Dual POV. On the road, the map reveals itself only to magical touch, showing a path to Crownforge beneath the fallen citadel of Vael. Rafael admits he can read it; Tamsin hides that she's seen it before. Rising unease: the map is choosing them.

chapters.title: The Free City of Dunmarrow
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. They reach Dunmarrow seeking supplies and find refugees from the border war Veyra's armies are winning. Tamsin's old smuggling contacts offer coin for the map. Temptation and guilt: survival has a price, and she nearly sells them out.

chapters.title: Hunters in Grey
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Veyra's grey-cloaked hunters ambush them in Dunmarrow's lower quarter. A mysterious swordsman, Oren, saves them but refuses to explain how he knew they'd be attacked. Paranoia takes root: someone is leaking their route.

chapters.title: Oren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Oren's POV. Oren reveals he served King Aldous before the crowning and believes the king still lives inside his own body, imprisoned. He joins them toward Crownforge. The beat is desperate hope — and the reader's first hint that Oren knows more about the Ember than he says.

chapters.title: The Pass of Hollow Bells
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Crossing the mountains, they find villages emptied by conscription, bells rung hollow by decree. Tamsin witnesses Rafael use forbidden magic to save a child, breaking his seven-year silence. Intimacy grows alongside fear of what he's becoming.

chapters.title: Letters from the Crown
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV (first antagonist chapter). From the occupied capital, Veyra senses the Ember stirring and dispatches her enforcer, Serah, offering a chilling glimpse of the usurper's certainty that she is saving the realm. The beat is seductive villainy: power justified as mercy.

chapters.title: Serah
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. The enforcer interrogates a captured smuggler and learns Tamsin's name — and her brother's connection to the map. She lets Tamsin's old debt be called in. Dread builds: the trap is already closing around the company.

chapters.title: The Debt Called In
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In the river town of Bray, Tamsin's creditors demand the map as payment or her life. Rafael pays with a charm that costs him a year of memory. Loyalty vs. truth sharpens: he trusts her completely; she cannot say why she doesn't deserve it.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Mark
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael discovers Oren communicating with Serah via a bound token and confronts him. Oren claims double agency — feeding false routes to protect them. Half the company believes him. Fractured trust; the middle's lowest point of unity.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Ford
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Serah's hunters strike at the river crossing. Oren fights on their side, seemingly proving himself, but Tamsin's brother's journal surfaces from her pack — revealing she has known the Ember's location all along. Betrayal cuts both ways.

chapters.title: Exile Within
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The company splits; Rafael and Tamsin press on alone, barely speaking. In a ruined shrine, the map shows Rafael a vision: the Ember is not a weapon but a fragment of the king's own soul, torn out at his crowning. Revelation reframes everything.

chapters.title: Crownforge Rising
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. They reach the fallen citadel of Vael and descend into Crownforge, finding Oren waiting — having cleared the way, or laid a trap. The approach to climax: awe, terror, and the sense of walking into a story older than themselves.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the Crown
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Serah arrives under truce and reveals the truth: Veyra is also bound — the Ember's removal created the thing that rules through Aldous, and killing the Ember frees neither king nor kingdom. Moral collapse of easy answers; Serah wavers.

chapters.title: Where the Crown Was Made
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. In Crownforge's heart, they find the Ember burning in its cradle and the ghost-echo of Aldous begging for release. Oren turns his blade — he wants the Ember for himself, believing it can restore the old dynasty through him. Climax begins.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael performs the unbinding, drawing the Ember into his own body as the forge collapses around them. He experiences the king's seven stolen years and Veyra's original grief. Sacrifice and transcendence: the price of survival paid in full.

chapters.title: Ash and Memory
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Rafael survives but has lost his memories of the journey — including her. Oren dies holding the collapsing gate; Sera defects, carrying proof of Veyra's binding to the free cities. Grief, tenderness, and the cost made personal.

chapters.title: The Council of Free Cities
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In Dunmarrow, Tamsin stands before the council and tells the whole truth — including her brother's death and her own lies — rather than the flattering version. Loyalty vs. truth resolved: honesty, not heroism, sways the cities to resist.

chapters.title: The Gate That Should Stay Shut
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. With fragmented memory, Rafael returns to the Ashgrove gate, now holding the Ember's power without knowing why it feels like home. Veyra's armies march; he must re-seal the gate against them using the Ember itself. Brink-of-war tension.

chapters.title: Emberlight
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the gate, the unbound king's remnant and Rafael's sacrifice break Veyra's binding; her armies falter as the truth reaches every soldier bound by the crown. Tamsin finds Rafael, a stranger who feels familiar, and introduces herself again. Resolution: bittersweet hope, a new beginning built on paid prices.
